note: Track seventh-shapes (guitar-extended-chords), step 2: the five open minor 7th and major 7th shapes, two as one finger off Am and C, three new, then strummed in time.

exercise.title: Open m7 and maj7 chords
exercise.why: Am7 and Cmaj7 are Am and C with one finger lifted, so each one is a shape you know with one more string ringing open.

cells.text: Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each chord as shown. Change from Am to Am7 and back, then from C to Cmaj7 and back, until only the one finger moves.

Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret Em7, Dm7 and Fmaj7 as shown. In Dm7, finger 1 lies flat across the two thinnest strings.
Pick the strings of each chord one at a time, and fix only the one that buzzes.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat.
Fingers 2 and 3 keep their shape from Cmaj7 to Fmaj7 and move over one string each.

Press Play below to start the metronome. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.
